artists.biography: The Sea Nymphs were an English psychedelic folk band from Kingston upon Thames, England, a side project by Tim Smith, Sarah Smith, and William D. Drake of the band Cardiacs. Their musical style is much lighter than that of their parent outfit, Cardiacs; the songs dispense with the use of loud guitars and drums, in favour of differing vocal rhythms, keyboards and brass instruments. However, the music still contains Cardiacs' trademark off-the-wall chord progressions and sudden time changes, albeit in a slightly gentler fashion. The group formed under the title Mr and Mrs Smith and Mr Drake, releasing a self-titled album in 1984. In 1991, group reunited and changed their name to The Sea Nymphs. They made their single debut with "Appealing to Venus" (1991), preceding their eponymous debut album (1992). Tim Smith suffered a cardiac arrest in 2008, limiting his mobility and temporarily causing the group to go on hiatus before returning to the studio in 2015 to complete the Sea Nymphs' second album On the Dry Land (2016), which was recorded around the same time as their debut in the 1990s but unfinished until that point. Tim Smith passed away from another heart attack in July 2020. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
On The Dry Land is the second studio album by the English band The Sea Nymphs, released in 2016 by The Alphabet Business Concern. Musically, the album blends elements of psychedelic folk, chamber pop, and art rock, characterized by gentle melodies, intricate arrangements, and a whimsical yet melancholic atmosphere. The instrumentation features acoustic guitars, keyboards, and layered vocals, creating a sound that is both intimate and otherworldly, reflecting the band's roots in the experimental rock group Cardiacs while exploring a more subdued and pastoral direction.

The album holds a unique place in The Sea Nymphs' discography, as it was recorded during the same sessions as their 1992 debut but remained unreleased for over two decades due to the health struggles of bandleader Tim Smith. Its eventual release in 2016 was met with critical acclaim, praised for its delicate songwriting and emotional depth. Reviewers noted its continuity with the band's earlier work, highlighting tracks like "Big River" and "Cut Yourself Kidding" for their lyrical charm and musical sophistication. On The Dry Land stands as a testament to the group's enduring creativity and is regarded as a significant addition to their catalog.
